categories.name: AI Content Systems
categories.strategy: Sell a constrained production or quality workflow rather than a promise to flood platforms with AI output. Reuse schemas and test fixtures, retain source provenance, and price human review explicitly.
categories.main_obstacle: The tool can produce quickly while fact-checking, rights clearance and distribution remain labor-intensive. Platform AI rules are not interchangeable.

categories.name: Video & Creator Media
categories.strategy: Original evergreen tutorials and reusable editing assets can support branded publishing. Compare a licensed asset product with an editing service before committing to an audience-only model.
categories.main_obstacle: Ad monetization has audience gates; repetitive mass production, reused footage and unapproved likenesses undermine eligibility and privacy.

categories.name: Audio, Music & Voice
categories.strategy: Favor original reusable sound packs and bounded batch-processing utilities. A reference-quality preview and rights manifest matter more than a large file count.
categories.main_obstacle: Voice consent, music/sample licences, loudness QA and ongoing editorial work can dominate costs. Do not promise imitation of unlicensed voices.

categories.name: Writing, Publishing & Newsletters
categories.strategy: Differentiate through useful information, tested examples and editorial credibility. A reusable guide can be low-touch; a frequently updated newsletter is a publishing job until retention supports delegation.
categories.main_obstacle: Generic generated books and recurring low-value summaries compete with free substitutes. Pen names do not eliminate tax, KYC or defamation exposure.

categories.name: SEO & Search-led Websites
categories.strategy: Sell a concrete diagnostic or decision utility first; build search traffic as an additional channel. Use original datasets or calculations rather than mass near-duplicate pages.
categories.main_obstacle: Ranking and traffic are uncertain and can change. Scaled-content or doorway abuse is not a scalable business advantage.

categories.name: Advertising & Marketing Analytics
categories.strategy: Read-only analysis and QA can begin as a paid diagnostic and evolve into recurring monitoring. Define attribution limits and one measurable problem per product.
categories.main_obstacle: Never equate correlated performance with guaranteed ad uplift. Managing live spend requires separate customer approval, costs and rollback.

categories.name: Email, CRM & Sales Enablement
categories.strategy: Build reusable checks, consent-aware workflows and document generators. Sell reduced administrative friction, not lists of unwilling recipients.
categories.main_obstacle: Consent, deliverability and private CRM data constrain automation. Purchasing a tool does not confer permission to send commercial messages.

categories.name: Social, Community & Memberships
categories.strategy: Use official integrations for bounded publishing workflows and sell operational resources or member utilities. Treat community moderation as a real recurring labor cost.
categories.main_obstacle: Audience acquisition, moderation and platform restrictions prevent fully passive operation. No fake engagement, reviews or impersonation.

categories.name: Digital Templates & Printables
categories.strategy: A specific repeatable task, an editable example and clear compatibility can justify a download price. Bundle coherent outputs instead of hundreds of interchangeable pages.
categories.main_obstacle: Delivery is easy to automate; copying, support and low discovery are not. Native marketplace acceptance can take time.

categories.name: Graphic Design & Brand Assets
categories.strategy: Sell original coherent systems with practical formats, accessible variants and licence clarity. A usable sample helps test whether buyers prefer the product to free assets.
categories.main_obstacle: Fonts, trademarks, stock restrictions and inconsistent AI acceptance matter. A reusable style system still needs art direction and QA.

categories.name: 3D, CAD & Digital Fabrication
categories.strategy: Prefer original non-safety-critical resources with tested dimensions, assembly or import instructions and source files. Paid maker tests should precede large packs.
categories.main_obstacle: Physical fit, material tolerances, machine safety and third-party design rights require human checks. Software familiarity is not a ranking bonus.

categories.name: Games & Interactive Entertainment
categories.strategy: Small finished experiences and production aids provide bounded tests. Reuse packaging and licensing while treating each audience as a separate acquisition problem.
categories.main_obstacle: Hit-driven demand, engine updates, refunds and substantial production effort make games weaker immediate cash-flow assumptions than their upside suggests.

categories.name: Education & Training
categories.strategy: Prefer an original, assessable learning outcome with worked solutions and a small paid test. License to organizations when the material truly solves a recurring training need.
categories.main_obstacle: Teaching expertise and accuracy cannot be outsourced blindly. No copyrighted test banks, academic cheating services or unsupported certification claims.

categories.name: Websites & Storefront Design
categories.strategy: Reusable tested components can be sold independently of bespoke site-building. Target one concrete integration or design gap and ship setup documentation.
categories.main_obstacle: A template marketplace is supply evidence, not buyers for your item. Security, accessibility, licensing and platform version support add work.

categories.name: SaaS & Business Applications
categories.strategy: Start with an accepted workflow and paid design partners, then build only the recurring part. Quotas, cancellation, tenant isolation and support need to exist before scale.
categories.main_obstacle: A recurring charge is not recurring value. Customer acquisition, churn, uptime and support can outweigh attractive software margins.

categories.name: Desktop & Mobile Utilities
categories.strategy: Local-first tools can reduce data exposure and server cost. Choose a narrow repeat-use problem, trial activation and a bounded compatibility promise.
categories.main_obstacle: Store identity disclosure, review, signing, device fragmentation and update obligations complicate apparent passivity.

categories.name: Plugins, Extensions & Connectors
categories.strategy: Build the smallest missing step in an existing workflow. Permission minimization and documented export paths create trust; read-only adapters reduce initial risk.
categories.main_obstacle: Platform changes and rejected permissions can break distribution. A source licence may permit internal use but not paid embedding or resale.

categories.name: Developer, DevOps & Testing
categories.strategy: Package a painful reproducible engineering task with fixtures, CLI outputs and regression tests. Sell a measurable saved step rather than a generic boilerplate dump.
categories.main_obstacle: Strong free alternatives and support across toolchains impose maintenance. Do not ship secrets or unsafe automatic production changes.

categories.name: APIs & Data Infrastructure
categories.strategy: Charge for reliability, normalization and bounded usage where free upstream data is inconvenient. Establish commercial data rights and an explicit unit-cost ceiling.
categories.main_obstacle: Abuse, hostile inputs, availability, exchange licences and API costs can erase margin. Usage revenue is not automatically high profit.

categories.name: Analytics, Reporting & Spreadsheets
categories.strategy: Reuse deterministic calculations and source reconciliation, first in a scoped paid job and later as a download or recurring report. Preserve the existing CSV service as one option.
categories.main_obstacle: Numbers need accepted definitions; sensitive data and custom exceptions limit passivity. The current prototype does not validate demand.

categories.name: Documents, Extraction & Workflow Automation
categories.strategy: A narrow known input family can support repeatable extraction, checking and document output. Add a human exception queue instead of promising universal automation.
categories.main_obstacle: OCR errors, ambiguous source documents, client confidentiality and orchestration licensing must be costed before selling a recurring plan.

categories.name: Ecommerce Product Operations
categories.strategy: Read-only preflight, reconciliation and specialized merchant utilities can be tested without editing a live store. Partner with agencies after repeated merchant demand.
categories.main_obstacle: Existing inexpensive apps cover generic tasks. Production catalog writes, returns and private customer data require strong controls.

categories.name: Print-on-demand & Physical Fulfillment
categories.strategy: Use original designs, order samples and test preorders before adding variants. Measure net margin after production, shipping, taxes, returns and acquisition.
categories.main_obstacle: Automated manufacturing does not remove working capital, quality defects or customer support. Avoid counterfeit or unlicensed fan merchandise.

categories.name: Directories, Jobs & Marketplaces
categories.strategy: Start with a tightly defined information or matching utility and manual verification. Monetize only when one side receives demonstrated value.
categories.main_obstacle: Two-sided cold starts, stale entries, privacy and scams make a generic directory or job board slow to monetize; never fabricate listings or demand.

categories.name: Research, Datasets & Information Products
categories.strategy: Sell a meaningful filter, quality check, normalized export or original analysis with provenance. Prefer lawful bulk/API sources over uncontrolled scraping.
categories.main_obstacle: Open access is not unlimited redistribution. False negatives, stale data and ongoing analyst time can be expensive.

categories.name: Finance & Bookkeeping Operations
categories.strategy: Keep initial products administrative: reconcile agreed exports, organize records and calculate explicitly defined scenarios. Leave filing, advice and regulated conclusions to qualified people.
categories.main_obstacle: Financial errors cause harm. Private banking records, tax scope and jurisdiction-specific rules make expert review and accurate disclaimers necessary.

categories.name: Stocks, Investing & Market Tools
categories.strategy: Separate selling a useful research tool from investing your own capital. Research aids need licensed data and non-misleading outputs; capital returns are not startup-business sales.
categories.main_obstacle: No promised returns or automated client-money execution. Advice, trade signals, data redistribution and capital loss require a separate review and no automatic launch.

categories.name: Privacy, Security & Compliance Tools
categories.strategy: Favor local inventory tools, evidence organization and permissioned read-only checks. Minimize what is collected and publish exact coverage instead of broad protection claims.
categories.main_obstacle: Never claim a tool guarantees security or legal compliance. Credentials, scan permission and professional responsibility make unsupervised operation inappropriate.

categories.name: Localization & Accessibility
categories.strategy: Deterministic technical checks, editorial QA and accessible production helpers can be reused across industries. State what the tests do and do not establish.
categories.main_obstacle: Technical checks do not certify linguistic accuracy or accessibility conformance. Disability-related claims and user data require care.

categories.name: Property, Construction & Home Services
categories.strategy: Administrative products can address repetitive work without making engineering, inspection or licensing decisions. One contractor or property-manager pilot should anchor a specific use case.
categories.main_obstacle: Safety-critical calculations, tenant privacy, local law and existing suites can block a generic quick-launch plan.

categories.name: Logistics, Manufacturing & Supply Chains
categories.strategy: Use bounded exports and exceptions to solve unit mismatches, fulfillment delays or inventory visibility. Read-only pilots avoid operational disruption.
categories.main_obstacle: Bad quantities, units or lead times can halt operations. Avoid automated machine control and safety-critical guidance without qualified oversight.

categories.name: Food, Hospitality & Travel
categories.strategy: Sell administrative workbooks, verified information or customer-owned content resources. Begin with one business workflow and an honest time-saved comparison.
categories.main_obstacle: Food safety, allergens, real-time travel data and venue policies are not safe to guess. Repeated local updates reduce passivity.

categories.name: Health & Wellness Administration
categories.strategy: Use fictional data and non-clinical administrative products first. Qualified privacy and domain review must precede handling patient information or affecting care.
categories.main_obstacle: A practice-operations market does not validate medical advice or diagnostic products. Do not automate treatment, triage or health outcome claims.

categories.name: People, HR & Recruitment
categories.strategy: Administrative automation and candidate-controlled resources can be bounded. Test an actual recruiter or HR workflow while retaining human hiring decisions.
categories.main_obstacle: Protected traits, fairness, applicant data, surveillance and employment law make autonomous selection and intrusive monitoring unsuitable.

categories.name: Agriculture, Environment & Energy
categories.strategy: Focus on records, educational planning and licensed-data summaries. Validate with operators before building integrations or extrapolating precision from uncertain inputs.
categories.main_obstacle: No pesticide, veterinary, electrical safety or unsupported carbon-credit advice. Hardware dependence and seasonal demand complicate automation.

categories.name: Nonprofits, Events & Public Services
categories.strategy: Reusable coordination, reporting and information tools can be brand-led. Sell to an authorized buyer and keep permissions, accessibility and records clear.
categories.main_obstacle: Charitable receipting, public procurement, children’s data, election operations and funding eligibility need specific review; no automated official decisions.

scope: Broad but finite; not every possible niche. One primary category plus industry and secondary-category facets. No preference for the owner's existing projects.
